title: Solvable Game
body_html:
Solvable Game

A game is solvable if the set $S^\infty$ of rationalizable outcomes is reduced to a singleton: $$ S^\infty=\{s^*\}. $$ This captures games whose common-rationality elimination process predicts a unique profile.

References

  • [MFoGT, Def. 4.4.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. A game is solvable if the rationalizable outcome set is a singleton.
  • [MFoGT, Section 1.3.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Earlier use of solvability for iterated elimination.

dependents.title: Solvable Games Have A Unique Nash Equilibrium

lean_refs.name: StrategicGame.IsDominanceSolvable
lean_refs.signature:
def IsDominanceSolvable (G : StrategicGame N U) : Prop :=
  ∃! σ : G.Profile, ∀ i, ∀ n, G.Survives n i (σ i)
lean_refs.docstring: A game is dominance-solvable if IESDS yields a unique surviving profile.
